answer: The ambiguity regarding the classification of predictive maintenance products as safety components under the AI Act is that it is unclear whether, if these products fail, classic quality assurance mechanisms will kick in. If these mechanisms do not activate upon failure, the products would presumably not be considered safety components. However, as trust in predictive maintenance products increases, it seems likely that redundant quality assurance mechanisms may be dismantled, which would then lead to these products being classified as safety components. This consideration is not adequately addressed by the AI Act.
